item.title: Physicists prove a long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization
item.description: **Problem:** Physicists saw hints of a universal speed limit on how fast quantum systems reach thermal equilibrium, but had no general proof. **Approach:** Paolo Abiuso and colleagues treated thermalization as a process and used quantum information theory to compute the fastest it can happen, testing on a model of interacting particles. **Result:** The minimum time is bounded by temperature and fundamental constants, independent of how hard the system is driven. Hotter means shorter allowed times; at very low temperature the gap between the two lowest energy states sets the limit. It ties to the Heisenberg limit. **Why it matters:** A fundamental constraint for designing quantum technologies, including quantum computers. **Glossary:** Thermal equilibrium (settled, uniform temperature); Qubit (quantum bit); Heisenberg limit (bound on measurement precision); Boltzmann constant (links temperature to energy).
